companyDescription: Superconducting quantum computing hardware + cloud access · Novera QPUs and Cepheus multi-chip systems · $497M cash, no debt · pending up-to-$100M Dept. of Commerce CHIPS award (LOI, equity-linked) · FY2026 revenue guided to ~$20M contingent on C-DAC system acceptance in Q4
priceNote: Live $11.52 (-5.2%) on Nov 11, 2026, the session after the Nov 10 Q3 print — down 34% from $17.51 at the Aug 10 report and roughly 75% below its 52-week high per B. Riley's Nov 2 note. Market cap ~$4.0B (~344M shares), now inside the turbo $5B ceiling. Old Base +45% ($25.39) is replaced by a new Base +30% ($14.98) anchored to the live price.
summary: Refresh after a -34% slide since the Aug 10 report and a weak Q3: revenue fell to $1.4M (vs $1.9M a year ago and a ~$3.5M estimate) on lumpy milestone and hardware-acceptance timing, though 9M revenue still doubled to $10.9M and cash held at $497M with no debt. Full-year 2026 revenue is guided to ~$20M, which needs customer acceptance of the C-DAC system and revenue recognition in Q4 — that is now the near-term proof point. The up-to-$100M Department of Commerce CHIPS award is still only a letter of intent (signed May 21), with the government taking an equity stake tied to the funding; no definitive agreement has been announced. Survival is clean, but the stock is a ~$4B company on ~$20M of revenue in a sector analysts are resetting (B. Riley cut to $25 on Nov 2), so this is a ค่าขนม position, not a Moonshot. Measured turbo median return to just after the catalyst is -10.6% (n=69): prefer the dip zone. Size 2% max.

catalysts.name: C-DAC System Acceptance → FY2026 ~$20M Revenue
catalysts.description: Management's ~$20M FY2026 revenue outlook assumes customer acceptance of the C-DAC system and revenue recognition in Q4 2026. With 9M revenue at $10.9M, Q4 needs roughly $9M — the acceptance is the swing factor.

catalysts.name: Dept. of Commerce $100M LOI → Definitive Agreement
catalysts.description: LOI signed May 21, 2026 for up to $100M over three years under the CHIPS Act, with Commerce receiving an equity stake tied to the amount awarded. Conversion to definitive agreements has no announced date.

catalysts.name: Q3 2026 Results
catalysts.description: Revenue $1.4M (miss vs ~$3.5M est.), operating loss $33.2M, GAAP net loss $3.1M on non-cash warrant/earn-out adjustments, cash $497M, no debt. Stock -5.2% the next session.

risks: Q3 revenue fell 27% YoY to $1.4M and missed estimates; revenue is lumpy and tied to a handful of hardware acceptances, so the ~$20M FY2026 guide depends on one Q4 customer acceptance (C-DAC).

~$4.0B market cap on ~$20M of annual revenue — valuation still rests almost entirely on the quantum-sector narrative, which is being reset (B. Riley cut RGTI to $25 from $35 and D-Wave to $27 from $40 on Nov 2).
The $100M Department of Commerce award is still an LOI; it may not convert, and if it does the government's equity stake dilutes existing holders.
Operating loss of $33.2M in Q3; the small GAAP loss was flattered by non-cash warrant and earn-out fair-value changes, not operations.
High correlation with IONQ, QBTS and LAES — sector-wide selling (including the Nov 5 semiconductor selloff) moves RGTI regardless of company news.

estimateDates.note: Needed for the ~$20M FY2026 revenue outlook
First read on whether the C-DAC acceptance landed

macroRisk.rateOutlook: The Fed hiked 25bp on Sep 16, 2026 (first hike since 2023), and a hot October CPI (core +0.3% m/m vs 0.2% expected) has pushed Dec 9 FOMC hike odds to roughly 89–100%, with the 10-year near 4.98%.
macroRisk.inflationNote: October CPI ran hot (headline +0.4% m/m, core +0.3%); October PCE on Nov 25 is the next inflation read.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: A ~$4B valuation on ~$20M of revenue is about as long-duration as equities get, so a priced-in December hike and a ~5% 10-year hit the multiple directly. Cash of $497M means no forced raise, but it does not protect the multiple.
macroRisk.summary: HIGH — rates are the main driver of quantum-sector multiples right now, and RGTI has no near-term earnings to anchor on; the clean balance sheet limits survival risk, not drawdown risk.

entryStrategy.verdict: SPECULATIVE — clean survival ($497M cash, no debt) but a Q3 revenue miss and a ~$4B valuation on ~$20M revenue; the next proof is C-DAC acceptance in Q4. Measured turbo median return from report price to just after the catalyst is -10.6% (n=69), so buying at report price is not the default: prefer $10.00–10.80. ค่าขนม sizing 2%.

catalystSpot.preRunup: partnership_win is the largest turbo bucket (n=32 complete, median excess vs SPY +7.3pp vs +7.7 overall — in line, not a laggard). RGTI's history shows sharp sector-wide runs on government-funding headlines rather than slow pre-event builds.
catalystSpot.preRunupTiming: Headline-driven — 1–3 days around government funding news

postWin.note: RGTI rose +9.3% in a single session in Aug 2026 on reports of U.S. government equity stakes in quantum firms; a definitive Commerce agreement would be a more concrete version of the same headline.

postLose.note: RGTI fell -4.4% after hours on its Aug 6, 2026 Q2 print and -5.2% the session after its Nov 10, 2026 Q3 miss (live-prices.json, Nov 11).

spotSizing.reason: Clean balance sheet, but the moon case needs both a sector re-rate and a funded government deal; ~$4B cap limits asymmetry, so the low end of the 2–5% band.

stopPostCatalyst.note: Exit if FY2026 revenue lands well below ~$20M (C-DAC not accepted) or the Commerce LOI is withdrawn
